text: WHO guideline: recommendations on digital interventions for health system strengthening.
note: Bibliographic reference title (WHO 2019 digital health guideline)

text: WHO SMART Guidelines: optimising country- level use of guideline recommendations in the digital age.
note: Bibliographic reference title (WHO SMART Guidelines article)

text: In response to requests from Member States for normative guidance on digital health, the World Health Organization (WHO) launched WHO guideline: recommendations on digital interventions for health system strengthening in 2019 (2).
note: Historical background on the 2019 launch of the WHO digital health guideline

text: Those evidence-based recommendations provide guidance to countries and regions looking to adopt digital health interventions as part of health system strengthening, and in support of universal health coverage or other health sector objectives.
note: Descriptive summary of the 2019 WHO digital health guideline's scope

text: In practice, for example, digital solutions that are built to support monitoring and evaluation programmes should not only serve the purpose of monitoring and evaluation, but should also bring value to the health worker.
note: Editorial illustration of Principles for Digital Development in Section 1.3

text: “Design with people” means that people who will manage, use, potentially benefit, and/or be affected by a given technology should meaningfully participate in the design of those systems so that the digital technology is built in a way that is fit-for-purpose (21).
note: Editorial explanation of 'Design with people' principle in Section 1.3
